ldo.desc: 3.3 V 1 A LDO with enable and active discharge, SOT-23-5 (DBV)
ldo.notes: STOCK: Active at DigiKey but 0 in stock there (backorder, 3,000 expected 14-Dec-2026, 26 week lead time). LCSC has 26,475 in stock. Findchips shows Arrow with 674 pcs (cut strips, Asia) and Verical with 674; no Mouser listing appeared in the Findchips result and mouser.com blocks scraping, so Mouser stock is unknown. So LCSC is the only place with real stock. ALTERNATE (same footprint and pinout): Diodes AP2112K-3.3TRG1, SOT-25, DigiKey AP2112K-3.3TRG1DICT-ND (Active, 406,515 in stock), LCSC C51118 (7,385 in stock), datasheet https://www.diodes.com/assets/Datasheets/AP2112.pdf. Read from the Diodes datasheet DS39724 Rev 2-2: SOT25 pins 1 VIN, 2 GND, 3 EN, 4 NC, 5 VOUT; output current 600 mA min; VIN recommended 2.5 V to 6.0 V (6.5 V absolute max); dropout for the 3.3 V version typ 125 mV / max 200 mV at 300 mA and typ 250 mV / max 400 mV at 600 mA; 'Stable with 1.0uF Flexible Cap: Ceramic, Tantalum and Aluminum Electrolytic', X5R or X7R recommended; output discharge 60 ohm when EN is low. Differences from the TLV757 to check against the design: 600 mA instead of 1 A, EN high threshold 1.5 V min instead of 1.0 V (EN low 0.4 V max, internal 3 Mohm pull-down), foldback short-circuit limit of 50 mA that can block start-up into a pre-existing current load, ambient rating -40 to 85 C, accuracy +/-1.5 %. TLV757 data from the first pass, datasheet SBVS322: VIN 1.45 V to 5.5 V. Dropout is specified only at 1 A: for DBV, 3.3 V <= VOUT < 5.0 V, typ 300 mV, max 425 mV (-40 to 85 C), max 475 mV (-40 to 125 C). No table value at 500 mA; linear scaling gives roughly 150 mV typ and under 240 mV max, which is an estimate, not a datasheet value. EN: VHI 1.0 V min, VLO 0.3 V max, EN current 10 nA. Output cap: 1 uF nominal minimum (0.47 uF effective after derating), 200 uF max, X5R/X7R ceramic; same minimum on the input. Active output discharge about 120 ohm typ.

rp2350.desc: RP2350A dual Cortex-M33/RISC-V MCU, A4 stepping (marked RP2350A0A4), QFN-60 7x7 mm
rp2350.notes: CHANGED from the candidate: SC1512 is the RP2354B code. RP2350A is SC1509 (7 inch reel, 500 pcs) and SC1509(13) (13 inch reel, 3400 pcs); the A4 stepping is ordered as SC1509-A4 and the chip is marked RP2350A0A4. DigiKey: SC1509-A4, Active, 6,933 in stock. Mouser 358-SC1509 was seen through a Findchips listing for SC1509-A4 (3,212 in stock), not on mouser.com itself. LCSC C42411118 is listed only as 'RP2350A' with 5,714 in stock and does not state the stepping, so ask PCBWay to source SC1509-A4 and check the A4 marking. Stepping: A4 is the production version; PCN 28 says mass production moved to A4 in July 2025 and all other variants are EOL. A DigiKey forum reply from January 2026 said some stock was still A2, so the -A4 suffix matters. E9: the Bank 0 GPIO pad leakage that defeated the internal pull-down on A2 is fixed in silicon from A3 and therefore in A4, so external pull-down resistors are no longer required. A4 needs Pico SDK 2.1.0 or newer (PCN says 2.1 or newer).

KiCad side, read from the library: footprint microSD_HC_Hirose_DM3AT-SF-PEJM5 has pads 1 to 8 in the rear row, pad 9 at the end of that row, pad 10 on the side edge, and four shell pads named SH. Symbol Micro_SD_Card_Det_Hirose_DM3AT (extends Micro_SD_Card_Det2) has 1 DAT2, 2 DAT3/CD, 3 CMD, 4 VDD, 5 CLK, 6 VSS, 7 DAT0, 8 DAT1, 9 DET_B, 10 DET_A, SH SHIELD. Symbol and footprint pad names agree with each other and pins 1 to 8 follow the standard microSD order. STILL OPEN: I have not verified against the Hirose drawing what the two detect pins do (which one is the switch contact, whether the other is common or tied to the shell, and whether it closes or opens on insertion). Do not rely on the detect polarity until someone reads the drawing.

rgb.desc: Addressable RGB LED with integrated driver, 2.0x2.0 mm, 12 mA per channel, rated for 3.3 V to 5.3 V supply
rgb.notes: CHANGED from WS2812B-2020 to WS2812B-2020-V6, which resolves the 3.3 V supply issue. Worldsemi does sell a 3.3 V rated version: its upgrade notice dated 30 Sep 2025 (https://www.tme.eu/Document/b595af8dc60cf69c7a13d19c3f98cb32/WS2812B+PCN.pdf) says the whole WS2812B series moves to the V6 suffix with the same protocol and package size, 'Constant-Current Drive at 3.3V', and that stock switches over immediately. Exact quotes from the V6 datasheet (English copy at https://files.waveshare.com/wiki/common/WS2812_0807.pdf): features list 'Static power consumption is below 1uA; 3.3 V power supply is supported.' and the ratings table row 'Power supply voltage | VDD | +3.3 ~ +5.3 | V'. Worldsemi's product page says '3.3V-5.5V'. Note that the datasheet prints this range in the Absolute Maximum Ratings table and 3.3 V is its lower edge, so a 3.3 V rail has no margin below nominal; the electrical tables are still specified at VDD = 5 V. Input levels: VIH min 0.55 VDD and VIL max 0.7 V in the datasheet (the notice says 0.6 VDD), so 3.3 V data works at either 3.3 V or 5 V supply. Pinout per the V6 datasheet pin table: 1 DO, 2 GND, 3 DI, 4 VDD, the same as the old part and as required. DI and DO are stated to be interchangeable on V6. KiCad symbol LED:WS2812B-2020 has 1 DOUT, 2 VSS, 3 DIN, 4 VDD and footprint LED_WS2812B-2020_PLCC4_2.0x2.0mm has pads 1 to 4, so numbers and functions agree. The V6 solder pad drawing is an image I could not read, so pad positions rest on Worldsemi's statement that the package size is unchanged. Sourcing: LCSC C52917434, 833,895 in stock; LCSC lists supply 3.3V~5.3V and height 0.84 mm. DigiKey and Mouser do not list Worldsemi parts. The old part WS2812B-2020 is LCSC C965555, 'Not available now', VDD +3.7 V to +5.3 V per datasheet V1.3 (https://cdn-shop.adafruit.com/product-files/4684/4684_WS2812B-2020_V1.3_EN.pdf).
